articles.title: When Is Quentin Grimes Coming Back? Lakers Announce Positive Injury Update
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers announced a Quentin Grimes injury update after the wing was listed as 'out' for Monday following a right finger sprain. The post When...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are without wing Quentin Grimes for the team's game against the Atlanta Hawks, as the free-agent addition suffered a finger injury in the Sunday night win over the Detroit Pistons. While there were initial concerns that Grimes' injury could cause a long-term absence, according to the latest updates, the Lakers aren't expecting him to miss a ton of time.

Grimes signed a four-year, $60 million deal with Los Angeles over the summer to become the team's fourth-highest-paid player. While he hasn't had a great start to the year, the Lakers would prefer him to be healthy and available on a nightly basis.

After Grimes suffered his finger injury in the Lakers' win over the Pistons, X-rays returned negative, and though he was ruled out for the team's Monday night game, the latest updates should signal good news for Los Angeles.

When Is Quentin Grimes Coming Back? Lakers Announce Positive Injury Update

For now, it is uncertain when Grimes will return from his injury for the Lakers. However, ahead of the team's game against the Hawks, head coach JJ Redick offered a positive update on his status.

"No worries," Redick said, per team reporter Benjamin Royer . "Just some swelling…So I think just being cautious with it, and hopefully he's back, you know, the next game or so."

Grimes went down with the finger injury on Sunday, leaving the game after scoring 12 points and dishing out four assists in 33 minutes.

"Quentin Grimes just went back to the Lakers locker room with a member of the medical staff," ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported.

After that win, Grimes had an X-ray on his finger, which came back negative. It was good news for a Lakers team that still needs all the help it can get out of its wings this season.

"Grimes banged a finger on his R hand, per the Lakers. X-rays taken at the arena came back negative," McMenamin added in a subsequent Grimes injury update.

Despite the positive injury news, Grimes was still listed on the Lakers' injury report as out for the game against the Hawks.

He is officially listed as 'out' due to a right finger sprain, but as Redick said in his latest Grimes injury update, it doesn't look like the player will be out for an extended period.

The Lakers have been cautious with other injuries so far this season, so it makes sense the team is playing the long game amid the hot start to the year.

Los Angeles' Key Free Agent Addition So Far This Season

As mentioned, Grimes signed with the Lakers for $60 million to become the fourth-highest-paid player on the team, only behind Luka Doncic , Austin Reaves , and Walker Kessler on the franchise's salary cap.

Before the season, there was an expectation he'd be the starting small forward, but so far this year, that's only been the case on one occasion when Doncic was sitting out. Instead, Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , and Jake LaRavia have all been the different starting forwards for the Purple and Gold, even though each is making significantly less money than the 26-year-old.

It's been a bit of a down campaign for Grimes so far, as through 11 games, Grimes is averaging eight points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.5 assists on 43.1/25.6/68.8 shooting splits in 25.9 minutes per appearance.

With his latest injury, this is the first game of the year Grimes has missed. However, as Redick said in his update on the wing, it doesn't look like he'll miss much time. Though Grimes hasn't necessarily been as advertised for the Lakers so far, he remains a key piece in the rotation, regardless of what his poor numbers might show.

Along with missing Grimes due to injury, Los Angeles is without Reaves on Monday night, as he sat out with an illness.

The next chance for both to return is in the team's next game on Wednesday, as the Lakers continue a four-game road trip to play the Milwaukee Bucks .

articles.title: Bills injury update: Is Dalton Kincaid playing in Week 9?
articles.summary: Dalton Kincaid will be helping the Bills against the Vikings in Week 9.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will host the Buffalo Bills in primetime in Week 9 as they play each other with a lot on the line. The Vikings lost their undefeated record in Week 8 to the Detroit Lions , so they will be looking to get back on track against arguably the best team in the NFL.

Both teams are dealing with a handful of injuries that could swing the matchup in one team's favor or the other. In this piece, we are discussing the status of Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid.

Kincaid has been active for Week 9 against the Bills. Through three quarters, he has been held to just two catches for 23 yards. Josh Allen always has his eyes on his security blanket, though, so he could make an impact at any time.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving combine for 78 points, erase 13-point Pacers lead in 125-122 Mavs' win
articles.summary: Pascal Siakam has monster first half but Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving were too much in a 125-122 Mavericks win over the Pacers
articles.body:
See the best photos from Pacers vs Mavericks

DALLAS -- Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving exploded for a combined 78 points to erase a 13-point Pacers lead and give the Mavericks a 125-122 win at the American Airlines Center on Monday night.

The Pacers fell to 3-8 with their second straight loss. The Mavericks improved to 7-4.

Flagg posted 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, grabbed 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving scored 35 points and hit on 7 of 10 3-pointers. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 29 points, 26 coming in the first half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, cener Ivica Zubac had 16 points. Kelly Oubre Jr. had 14.

Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving go berserk on Pacers

The Pacers corrected a lot of their problems from Saturday's loss to the Nuggets. They had a much stronger first-half performance. They shared the ball, shot it reasonably well and fought on the defensive end. But they simply had no antidote for one of the most potent starting backcourts in the NBA on a night when both of its members were sizzling.

Irving and Flagg, both former No. 1 picks out of Duke, hit inferno levels against the Pacers and produced more than half of the Mavericks' total production. They combined for 78 points on 27 of 43 shooting including 10 of 16 from 3-point range.

Flagg, the 6-9 wing functioning as a shooting guard -- and a great one -- scored 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range, and also hit 8 of 8 free throws. He added 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving, the 15-year veteran and nine-time All-Star, had a vintage performance that showed little evidence of his ACL tear last year. He finished with 35 points on 11 of 18 shooting including a shimmering 7 of 10 from 3-point range.

The Pacers hung around long enough to have a chance in the final minute, but late buckets by Flagg put the game away. He answered three Aaron Nesmith foul shots with a critical jumper to put the Mavericks up four with 1:02 to play. Then after a Nesmith 3-pointer, he hit a jumper on offensive rebound by Naji Marshall off Marshall's own missed free throw to put the Mavs up three with 26 seconds left. Two key free throws by Irving helped the Mavericks put the game away.

Pascal Siakam brilliant in first half, swarmed in second

With Tyrese Haliburton still out, the Pacers have been in need of something next level from Siakam to carry the squad. He's been solid throughout the Pacers' tough start and entered Monday averaging 21.4 points per game on 51.7% shooting, but he hadn't scored 30 points since the season opening win over the Pelicans and had only surpassed 25 points twice all season. It was even more imperative because they were up against Irving and Flagg.

Siakam certainly gave the Pacers everything they could have asked for in the first half. He hit his first eight field goals and his first five 3-pointers before finally missing a heat-check 3 in the final minutes of the second quarter. At the break he had 26 points on 8 of 9 shooting, six rebounds, four assists, no turnovers and no fouls, posting a +15 plus-minus figure in just 16 minutes of game action. In the second half, however he was swarmed with constant double and triple teams and scored just three points on 1 of 7 shooting.

Kelly Oubre Jr. gives one of his best efforts

The Pacers have been waiting for a breakout game from off-season free-agent signing Kelly Oubre Jr. as he entered Monday's game averaging just 8.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, shooting 41% from the floor and just over 23% from 3-point range. There's still certainly another level the Pacers would still like to see, but Monday's performance was a step in the right direction on both ends.

The long-armed 6-8 wing scored 14 points on 6 of 9 shooting including 1 of 3 from 3-point range. He had two rebounds but also gave the Pacers a defensive option off the bench they could use on Irving, Flagg and others.

Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Pacers Insider newsletter .
